scope.coverageNote: Scores evaluate the documented, explicitly scoped evidence. They do not certify all historical chat answers or all files in the workspace. Earlier AINOTE purchase/comparison answers were not available as assistant messages in the supplied history; no blanket correctness claim is made for them.

criteria.result: APK identity is consistent. All 115 catalog source hashes independently matched the saved Java sources; function and parameter IDs/reverse references were intact.
BLE/GATT, header offsets, little-/big-endian distinctions, m07 audio layouts, Wi-Fi transfer distinction and battery CRC fixture matched the inspected code.
Context-specific names and String/boolean autotts distinction are preserved, but float fields are assigned to object and profile-specific parser schemas are omitted.

criteria.criterion: Wire data versus internal application models
criteria.result: Automatic schema attribution promotes constructed Java fields into claimed wire paths; this affects work state, state info and file lists.

criteria.criterion: Function input, result, event and error contracts
criteria.result: Dispatch branches and source excerpts are useful, but all 443 Flutter entries have empty outputParameterIds. Known OTA event fields and error states are not described as separate result contracts.
gRPC/TLS, custom JSON-plus-buffer marshalling, routes and token/header roles are separated from model identity; no unsupported exact LLM or X-sign algorithm is asserted.
No firmware image is claimed recovered; AOT route strings, OTA handlers, private Android storage and signature/encryption distinctions are correctly qualified.

criteria.criterion: Consistency across earlier and newer documents
criteria.result: Older research-stage claims remain unmarked as superseded; candidate channel lists are labelled complete contracts in some reports.
Five principal pages and deep links loaded without JS errors. IDs, parameter/function reverse links and stored source hashes passed independent read-only checks.
Hardware/cloud non-validation, internal/official SDK distinction and lack of original C++/Dart/firmware sources are clearly disclosed; this audit additionally records limits of historical coverage.

findings.title: Constructed Java models are represented as JSON wire response schemas
affected: tools/catalog-extract.cjs: response parsing block; schemaLinks on class-name occurrence

evidence.detail: Reads errCode, workState, type, then constructs WorkState(i37, v6(i37), iOptInt). msg is generated locally; state is the Java representation of workState.
msg/state/type are Java fields without an observed wire-deserialization operation here.

70400 reads pageNum,totalFiles,data; data may be an array or a string containing JSON. Each entry reads name,fileType,fileList. FileListResponse.pageSize is arrayList.size(); DeviceFileInfo fields are constructed with local defaults.
create() calls DeviceInfoParsers and converts the typed glasses/headset result to a legacy StateInfo. Legacy stateL/stateR/master are not the glasses wire schema.

findings.impact: A client generated from schemaPaths would expect keys or paths never read from the glasses, and miss the actual nested layout.
findings.correction: Keep wire fields/paths, callback results, internal models and derived fields in distinct namespaces. Follow actual JSONObject/Gson/toMap parsing/serialization before assigning schemaPaths. Remove class-mention-only attribution. Model arrays and JSON-string alternatives explicitly.

findings.title: Float parameters are classified as object/reference values

evidence.detail: translate_sdk.TrackPlayer.playbackSpeedRate and two float method arguments have javaType=float, valueClass=număr real, but valueClassId=object. CLASE_VALORI has no real-number category.

findings.impact: Filtering and value-class descriptions give the wrong representation for these inputs.
findings.correction: Add a floating-point value class with Java binary32/binary64 storage semantics and JSON finite-number caveat; map float/double/Float/Double to it and validate the mapping.

findings.title: Profile-specific battery/system/version/state parser contracts are omitted

evidence.detail: parseBatteryInfo reads glasses bat with battery fallback and batChanging with charging fallback; parseStateInfo reads state; parseSystemInfo reads sn/mac; parseVersionInfo reads version. Headset branches are explicitly separate.
The detailed schemas contain no .bean.glasses. entries; the three named commands have outputParameterIds=[] in round 1.

findings.impact: The most basic glasses queries lack known result parameters while legacy/internal models are included elsewhere.
findings.correction: Include relevant common/glasses/headset types and actual DeviceInfoParsers paths. Link profile-specific results and transformations to the commands; do not equate internal model field names with wire keys.

findings.title: Known asynchronous Flutter result/event fields are not catalogued

evidence.detail: startGlassOTA takes path/otaVer, immediately acknowledges through Result.success(new HashMap()), then emits maps on the event sink. Event fields include type/status/message/progress. Known status values are -1 enter error, 0 connect, 1 start and 3 check success; type includes status,error,ota_progress,success. onOTACheckError forwards another dynamic status.
In round 1 all 443 Flutter entries have outputParameterIds=[]; startGlassOTA.errors=[] despite this available callback contract.

findings.impact: The catalogue exposes source excerpts but does not provide the requested structured output parameters, event variants and error meaning for a central operation.
findings.correction: Separate synchronous MethodChannel acknowledgement from asynchronous EventChannel/callback messages. Catalogue fields, discriminators, observed values and conditional omissions from each real producer; do not infer operation success from Result.success alone. Generalize safely across relevant recorded branches.

findings.title: Historical research claims and complete-contract labels conflict with later results

evidence.detail: Raport_SDK says binaries were not decompiled and no GATT UUIDs were identified. Later documents do identify/decompile them, but the early report is not clearly marked as a historical stage.

The channel inventory contains candidate method/event/enum strings and unresolved entries, so 'complete contracts' overstates what that inventory represents, even though a nearby caveat partially qualifies it.

findings.impact: Readers entering through an older report can conclude that the known protocol/SDK analysis has not been done, or mistake a string inventory for an invocable API specification.
findings.correction: Preserve historical reports but add prominent stage/supersession notes and links to the current verified reports. Replace 'complete contracts' with 'channel/argument candidate inventory' or equivalent accurate wording. Update generator templates as well as generated copies.
